dedupe_keys.name: mobile network hardening program mnhp funded base stations australia

description: The Mobile Network Hardening Program is an Australian Government programme that helps mobile network operators and infrastructure providers make regional mobile infrastructure more resilient: to prevent outages in natural disasters, to keep facilities running longer during bushfires and other disasters, and to restore service quickly after an outage. Round 1, funded through the Strengthening Telecommunications Against Natural Disasters initiative announced in January 2020, provides 23.5 million Australian dollars to Optus, Telstra and TPG for about 1,000 projects in two stages. Stage 1 extends battery backup to at least 12 hours at 466 base stations built under the first two rounds of the Mobile Black Spot Program; stage 2 funds more than 530 upgrades at base stations across Australia, including new portable and permanent generators, better transmission resilience within regional clusters to remove single points of failure, and new or upgraded batteries. The department publishes the funded base stations for both stages as open geodata. Coverage: regional Australia, round 1 (from 2020). Format and access: KML files per stage, WMS, WFS and GeoJSON from data.gov.au, free under CC BY-SA 4.0. Caveats: the data show funded sites and upgrade types, not measured outage performance; later rounds, if any, may be published separately. Simulation uses: backup power duration and single points of failure for mobile networks in bushfire and storm scenarios, cascading effects of power loss on communications, and restoration planning. Related records: the Mobile Black Spot Program case study covers the base stations these upgrades harden, and the Optus outage review shows national-scale failure.
